summary: 2 Samuel 2 (32 verses) continues the story of covenant with David. Starting with 'After this, David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?” Yahweh said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?” H', it moves through themes of covenant with David, fall and mercy and calls readers toward fall and mercy.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows covenant with David lived out in david's reign. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: After this, David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah?” Yahweh said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?” He said, “To Hebron.”
The battle was very severe that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before David’s servants.
They took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men went all night, and the day broke on them at Hebron.

questions.question: What is happening in 2 Samuel 2?
questions.answer: In 32 verses, this chapter 2 samuel 2 (32 verses) continues the story of covenant with david. starting with 'after this, david inquired of yahweh, saying, “shall i go up into any of the cities of judah?” yahweh said to him, “go up.” david said, “where shall i go up?” h', it moves through themes of covenant with david, fall and mercy and calls readers toward fall and mercy. The setting is david's reign, written to israel. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote 2 Samuel and why 2 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally prophetic history, addressed to israel around ~1000-960 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as court history — its themes of covenant with David, fall and mercy build on what came before.

questions.question: Are there any difficult words here?
questions.answer: Scan for names, places, or repeated abstract words like righteousness, covenant, or glory. The glossary below defines up to 3 that show up most. Ask: who is this person, what does this word mean in everyday terms?

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through covenant with David and fall and mercy, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 23 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'However, he refused to turn away. Therefore Abner with the back end of the spear struck him in the body, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there and died in t...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about covenant with David. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
